name: Eurorack power (Doepfer bus, 16 & 10 pin)
standard: Doepfer A-100 bus (de facto Eurorack standard)
ascii:
16-pin (2x8)              10-pin (2x5, power only)
   .----------.              .----------.
   | o      o | Gate         | o      o | +12V
   | o      o | CV           | o      o | GND
   | o      o | +5V          | o      o | GND
   | o      o | +12V         | o      o | GND
   | o      o | GND          | o      o | -12V  <red stripe>
   | o      o | GND          '----------'
   | o      o | GND
   | o      o | -12V  <red stripe>
   '----------'
   Red stripe = -12V on BOTH. Each row's two pins are the same
   rail. The 10-pin is the 16-pin's bottom five rows; it drops
   +5V, CV, and Gate.
description: The power connector that feeds every Eurorack module from the case bus board. Two forms: a 16-pin (2x8) header carrying the full bus (+/-12V, GND, +5V, CV, Gate) and the far more common 10-pin (2x5) header carrying just the power rails (+/-12V + GND). Each horizontal row's two pins are the same rail (the bus shorts them). The ribbon cable's red stripe marks -12V and must align to the module's -12V edge; get it backwards and the module is destroyed.

contacts.name: -12V
contacts.description: negative rail -- the RED STRIPE conductor; align this to the module's -12V mark

contacts.name: +5V
contacts.description: +5V bus (16-pin only; often absent on the bus board -- do not rely on it)

contacts.name: CV
contacts.description: CV bus (16-pin only; legacy, rarely used)

contacts.name: Gate
contacts.description: Gate bus (16-pin only; legacy, rarely used)

variants: 10-pin (2x5): the power-only subset = the bottom five rows of the 16-pin (-12V, GND, GND, GND, +12V). It drops +5V, CV, and Gate. Most modern modules use the 10-pin; a 10-to-16 ribbon plugs a 10-pin module onto a 16-pin bus header.

The three extra 16-pin signals (+5V, CV, Gate) are optional. +5V is frequently NOT wired on the bus board (add a dedicated +5V supply if a module needs it), and the CV/Gate buses are a legacy feature almost nobody uses now.
gotchas: Reversing the ribbon feeds -12V into +12V and vice-versa = INSTANT module destruction. The red stripe MUST go to -12V. Boxed (shrouded) headers key it so the ribbon can only seat one way; bare unshrouded pin headers do not -- triple check those.
Each row's two pins are the SAME rail (shorted on the bus), so a 16-pin connector distributes 5-6 signals, not 16 independent ones.
Do not assume +5V is available -- many bus boards leave it unconnected. A module needing +5V should regulate it locally from +12V or use a bus board that supplies it.

This connector just delivers the rails. What a well-designed module does next -- keyed connector, series Schottky reverse-protection, a 10R (or ferrite) + reservoir/decoupling caps per rail -- is the important part; see the eurorack-power-protection reference.
notes: Pinout verified from Noise Engineering's 'Standard Eurorack power connections' diagram (16 & 10 pin, signal-per-row). Pin 1 = -12V (red stripe) by IDC/Eurorack convention; the exact 1-vs-16 numbering follows the red-stripe / keyed edge. 10-pin = the -12V/GND/+12V subset.
